newsitem.title: USA: Wash. state jobless rate drops to 4.5 pct in May.
newsitem.headline: Wash. state jobless rate drops to 4.5 pct in May.

text.p: Washington state's jobless rate fell in May to 4.5 percent, almost two percentage points less than a year ago, the state said Tuesday.
Nonfarm employment jumped by 26,900 workers over the month, the state's Employment Security Department said.

Manufacturing payrolls expanded by 4,100 with sizable seasonal increases in lumber and wood products, and food processing. Textiles and apparel added 300 workers, while industrial machinery added 200 workers, the state said.
Aircraft and parts increased by 1,100 workers, bringing the cumulative five month job gain to 5,300. Construction increased by 3,700 workers as spring-time work activity heightened, the state said.

"Strong over-the-year growth, especially in the central Puget Sound area, coupled with normal seasonal upswings in agriculture, construction, services, and trade spurred the economy forward," Employment Security Commissioner Carver Gayton said in a statement.
